prerequisites: Basic knowledge of fundamentals of Mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the real operating characteristics and performance of power generation systems and the main prime movers used today.
Acquire specific knowledge for assessing real thermodynamic transformations, for calculating thermodynamic parameters and heat and work exchanges with reference to real cases.
Be familiar with the problems, limitations, advantages, and disadvantages of the considered power plants and their main components in real operating conditions.
Calculate the performance parameters of engines, with particular reference to efficiency and specific fuel consumption.

Define the behavior of real thermodynamic transformations occurring in power plants and their components in order to qualitatively and quantitatively evaluate the thermodynamic states and real transformations, as well as identify solutions to improve performance.

Critically evaluate and compare different solutions for implementing real energy conversion processes in power systems, taking into account the real behavior of transformations and processes, while also considering possible alternatives.

Effectively present evaluations and comparisons of different solutions for implementing energy conversion processes in power plants, through both graphical and numerical representations of the real thermodynamic transformations and cycles, as well as the main performance parameters commonly used.

Independently get information, characteristics, and technical data on Energy Systems that can be studied and/or available on the market, thus improving own skills on the solutions proposed and/or applied for the implementation and management of Energy Systems.

syllabus_topics: Energy Systems and Fluid Machines: classification and components
Review of Thermodynamics
Fundamental equations: mass and energy conservation; momentum and moment of momentum equations
Application to fluid flow in fixed and moving channels
Ideal, Limit, and Real thermodynamic cycles
Overview of Energy costs and utilization factors
Compressible Fluid Machines
Compression and expansion processes on thermodynamic diagrams; compression and expansion efficiencies
Total and stagnation quantities
Fluid Flow in fixed channels: converging channels, converging-diverging channels
Velocity and pressure trends, sonic and choking conditions
Steam Engines
Real Cycles: thermodynamic transformations in real Rankine cycles with saturated and superheated steam; performance calculation for reheated and regenerated steam plants in real operation
Steam generators: types and schemes; efficiency
Superheaters and economizers
Air preheaters
Condenser and cooling towers
Reciprocating internal combustion engines (ICEs)
Limit thermodynamic cycles: an overview of calculation methodology
Real thermodynamic cycles: trends of real transformations and main causes of deviation from the ideal case
Indicated cycle and calculation of effective power in internal combustion engines
Mean effective pressure
Volumetric efficiency
Overview of combustion processes
Air and fuel supply processes in ICEs
Mechanical supercharging and turbocharging
Characteristic curves
Gas turbines: thermodynamic processes in the Joule cycle in the limit and real cases
Real thermodynamic cycles on the (h, s) and (T, s) diagrams; effective specific work, effective power, and thermodynamic efficiency in limit and real Joule cycle
Effect of compression ratio and maximum cycle temperature
Turbine inlet temperature (TIT) and air-fuel ratio: effects on efficiency
Optimization of the real Joule cycle with reference to specific work and efficiency
Internal and External Combustion Plants
Components of Energy Systems
Thermodynamics reminders: closed and open systems, Heat Exchangers and Fluid Machinery
Application of conservation equations to fluid flow in fixed and moving channels
Thermodynamic cycles and pseudo-cycles: thermodynamic transformations, work and heat exchange calculation
Overview on energy cost and utilization coefficient
Real and ideal transformations
Recovery and counter-recovery phenomena
Intercooled and post-combustion compression
Fluid flow in fixed-wall ducts: converging ducts, converging-diverging ducts
Evaluation of velocity and pressure trends with a 1-D approach
Valves and pressure reducers
Notes on fluid flow in moving channels
Steam power plants: overview of the most common system configurations
Regeneration and reheating: real thermodynamic cycles on the (h, s) and (T, s) diagrams
Performance calculation of simple, reheated, and regenerated steam power plants in real situations
Steam generator efficiency: direct and indirect calculations
The deaerator
Reciprocating internal combustion engines (ICEs). Review of operating principles and fundamental components
Time losses, heat exchange, pressure drops through intake and exhaust valves and throttle valve
Overview of combustion processes in spark-ignition and Diesel engines
Air and fuel supply processes in ICEs: intake and exhaust systems and polar diagram of ideal and real valves timing
Characteristic curves of internal combustion engines
Gas turbines: an overview of the most common configurations
Introduction to blade cooling
Introduction to combustion chamber geometry
teaching_methods: Presentation of quantitative examples of specific power plants and calculation procedures
Teacher availability for clarifications and explanations by appointment (in person and online via Teams)

assessment_methods.method: Oral interview (two questions on course topics and application to original problems)

assessment_rules: The final exam consists of an oral interview with two questions. Each question is assessed on a scale from 0 to 30. A partial score of at least 18/30 is required for both questions to pass. The final score is the arithmetic mean of the scores of the two questions.
